current_answer: Choose by the frontend bottleneck and proof path: OpenAI Frontend App Builder for a new visual surface only when you can create and approve an Image Gen concept and compare a browser render; Anthropic Frontend Design for text-led visual direction; PracticalSwan Frontend Design 2.0 for a substantial product surface that needs an explicit task, state model, responsive checks, and rendered verification; Wenkang Frontend Design for a real route or defined concept where you need a local, project-derived preview to make visual decisions and export them back to Codex; Vercel React Composition Patterns for a flag-heavy React component; Vercel React View Transitions for meaningful interface motion; Agent Browser 0.38.1 for a runnable UI whose states you need to navigate, inspect, and capture; Agent Browser Dogfood 0.38.1 for exploratory QA that must leave reproducible browser evidence; OpenAI Frontend Testing & Debugging for a named rendered change or bug flow when the Build Web Apps plugin and a documented Browser or allowed fallback path are available; OpenAI Product Design Audit for a real user flow you can capture and review; Vercel Web Design Guidelines for a code-first UI review; and Vercel React Best Practices for React or Next.js performance. A local preview is not proof of the live route. Browser evidence needs its proof surface: backend, viewport, target URL, session context, and visible state. Eleven listings are source-pinned; Frontend Testing & Debugging is a mutable current source with Build Web Apps manifest version 0.1.2, not a skill-file pin. None has been independently result-tested by this pool.
